title: The 5 Buildings That Took Longest to Finish, Ranked (#1 Beat 632 Years)

scenes.text: The five buildings that took longest to finish. Number one took longer than the United States has existed.
Number five: St Peter's Basilica in Rome. 120 years, 1506 to 1626. Michelangelo designed its dome and never saw it built.
scenes.label: St Peter's · 120 years

scenes.text: Number four: the Sagrada Familia in Barcelona. Begun in 1882, its tallest tower was only topped in 2026, 144 years later. The entrance still isn't done.
scenes.label: Sagrada Familia · 144 years

scenes.text: Number three: York Minster in England. 252 years, 1220 to 1472, for one of the largest medieval cathedrals in northern Europe.
scenes.label: York Minster · 252 years

scenes.text: Number two: Milan Cathedral. First stone 1386. The last bronze door went in in 1965, almost 580 years later.
scenes.label: Milan Cathedral · 580 years

scenes.text: Number one: Cologne Cathedral. Started 1248, finished 1880: 632 years, with a 284-year pause and a medieval wooden crane left on the half-built tower. The United States is 250.
scenes.label: Cologne Cathedral · 632 years

description:
The five buildings that took longest to complete, ranked by years from first stone to completion.
St Peter's Basilica took 120 years (1506 to 1626); Barcelona's Sagrada Familia, begun in 1882, topped out its central tower in 2026 with work on the Glory facade still under way; York Minster took 252 years (1220 to 1472); Milan Cathedral was begun in 1386 and declared complete when its last bronze door was installed in 1965; and Cologne Cathedral, started in 1248, stood unfinished from 1560 to 1842 with a medieval timber crane on its south tower before being completed in 1880, 632 years after the first stone.
Which one would you have waited for, and what should we rank next?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one? Stonehenge was built in stages over roughly 1,500 years, but it was never one continuous project. What should we rank next?
